about: RootVine's word-match rule: is the song a live lookup resolved to a real answer for the words asked? Shared with BeatsVine's demand ledger (agreed 2026-09-26), which counts an ask only when this rule passes. Source of truth: RootVine src/suggest.ts, similarity(...).strong. `asked` is the slug RootVine sends to BeatsVine's live lookup; `title` and `artist` are what the lookup resolved to. Change the rule on either side only with this file.
rule: Words: the slug's hyphen-separated words, folded like BeatsVine's slugify (lowercase, Latin accents removed, apostrophes dropped: don't = dont). The resolved title and artist are folded the same way, splitting on spaces, hyphens and symbols.
Glue words never count on either side: the a an by and feat ft featuring x vs with on to for is it (unless a name is nothing but glue, when its words are kept).

Optional words need not match (but count when they do): song songs track tracks single album albums lp ep vinyl cd cds record records cassette music, and years 1900-2099. If every asked word is optional, they are all required.

Two words are the same when equal, or, for Latin letters only and words of 4+ letters, at most 1 edit apart (2 for 8+ letters); swapping two neighbouring letters is one edit. Digits and non-Latin scripts must match exactly.

Strong when all of: at least 60% of the non-optional asked words appear in title + artist; at least one title word is matched by an asked word that is not part of the artist's name; and, if only one non-optional word was asked, every title word was asked.
